title: He sees the look on your face before you ask
subtitle: Al-Basir: the All-Seeing, whose sight misses nothing and understands everything
intro: Al-Basir (الْبَصِيرُ) means the All-Seeing: the One who sees everything in creation, the smallest ant on a black rock in a dark night, every hidden act and every state of the heart, and who sees with full insight into what it means. It means nothing you go through is invisible, and every good you do in private is witnessed.

root.sense: Basar is eyesight, and basirah is insight, seeing into the heart of a matter. The root joins both: to see a thing and to understand it. Al-Basir sees every outward detail and also perceives its inner reality, with a sight that needs no eye, light or distance.

row.title: Ihsan
sub: living as one who is seen

knowing: Al-Basir sees everything, near and far, large and small, open and hidden, all at once. Scholars like to say He sees the black ant crawling on a black rock on a moonless night. {idea}Darkness, walls and distance mean nothing to His sight.{/idea} And He sees more than surfaces: He sees what a deed looks like from the inside, whether it was done for Him or for an audience.

Three names can sound alike here. Al-Basir is His sight itself: nothing that exists escapes it. Ar-Raqib is His continuous watch over you, guarding and keeping account. Ash-Shahid is His presence and testimony: He witnesses everything and will bear witness to it. Al-Basir is the root of the other two: because He sees, He watches over you, and because He sees, His testimony is true.

Like His hearing, His sight is real and perfect, and it is not like ours. There is nothing like Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing (42:11). Ours needs light, eyes and a line of sight, and it tires and fails. His never does.
seeing: Before the qiblah changed, the Prophet ﷺ longed to face the Kaaba in prayer but did not ask aloud. He would only look up at the sky. Allah said: We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, and We will turn you to a qiblah that will please you (2:144). {reward}He saw a longing that was never put into words, and answered it.{/reward}

Allah comforted the Prophet ﷺ in hard days with the words: be patient, for you are before Our eyes (52:48). He reminded him of the One who sees him when he stands in prayer and his movement among those who prostrate (26:218-219). When Musa was afraid of Pharaoh, Allah said: I am with you both; I hear and I see (20:46). His sight is not surveillance from a distance. It is care up close.
Look at the birds above you, wings spread and folded. Who holds them up? Only the Most Merciful, for He sees all things (67:19). Every creature is held in His sight at every moment.
trusting: When you are wronged and no camera caught it, when you are struggling and no one notices, Al-Basir saw it. {reward}You do not need a witness or a recording to be believed by Him.{/reward} The carer whose nights no one sees, the worker whose honesty no one rewards, the child quietly holding a family together: all of it is in His sight.

His sight also gives quiet strength in hardship. If He sees what you are going through, then what you are going through is not random and not forgotten. He is patient with you, and He gives in His time, the way He saw the Prophet's face and answered.

And it reshapes your private life. Most of us have a gap between how we act in public and how we act alone. {trap}Feeling relief that no one saw a wrong{/trap} is a sign this name has not yet settled in the heart. The Prophet ﷺ described the highest level of faith, ihsan, as worshipping Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, knowing that He sees you (Sahih Muslim). The aim is not fear of being caught, but the dignity of living well in front of the One who loves you.
loving: We all want to be seen, truly seen, not just glanced at. Al-Basir sees you with complete clarity: your effort, your fear, your hidden goodness. {idea}You are never invisible to the One whose look is full of mercy.{/idea}

There is also something beautiful in wanting to look good for Him. We dress well for guests and inspectors. When you start to beautify your private moments for His sake, worship becomes a kind of love.
now: It is 6am on a night shift, you are cleaning up after a patient who will never remember your name, and nobody on the ward noticed the extra care you took. {reward}Al-Basir saw every gentle movement of your hands.{/reward} You were working in front of the only audience that matters.
old: What I do when nobody is watching does not really count.
new: Al-Basir sees every unseen kindness and every private struggle, so my hidden life matters most of all.
try: Pick one thing you do differently when alone, and today do it as if you were in full view of Al-Basir.

dua.text: Ya Basir, You see me when I stand and when I fall. Let me be, in private, the person I want You to see, and look upon me with mercy.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name when you feel unseen or are tempted in private; Musa was reassured with the words I hear and I see (20:46).

pairs.why: As-Sami' hears every word, Al-Basir sees every act and look; the Quran joins them again and again to show His complete attention.
Al-Basir is His sight, Ar-Raqib is His constant watch over you to protect and keep account; one is seeing, the other is watching over.
Al-Basir sees what happens; Al-Khabir knows the hidden reality behind it. Together they leave nothing outside His grasp (17:30).

faq.a: Al-Basir means the All-Seeing. Allah sees everything in existence, outward and hidden, near and far, at every moment, and He sees with full insight into its reality. His sight is real and perfect and does not resemble the sight of any creature.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Basir, Ar-Raqib and Ash-Shahid?
faq.a: Al-Basir is His sight: nothing escapes it. Ar-Raqib is His constant watchfulness over His creation, guarding it and keeping account. Ash-Shahid is His presence and witness: He is present to every event and will testify to its truth. All three rest on His perfect sight and knowledge.

faq.q: What is ihsan and how is it related to Al-Basir?
faq.a: In the well-known hadith of Jibril in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ defined ihsan as worshipping Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, knowing that He sees you. Living with the name Al-Basir is the path to ihsan.
